thread:
maya: starting onboarding thread for nova-13b-c (Dedicated). primary asks: pick a quant path (int8 PTQ, fp8 native, or gguf hybrid), define smoke checklist, and owners. target: ~2x token-cost reduction and <=3% absolute quality drop vs fp16. who can own runs + docs?

jordan: baseline first: run fp16 eval to lock reference metrics (eval suites + cost/latency). then int8 PTQ with ~512-1024 calib samples, per-layer histogram if possible. measure PPL, EM/ROUGE on benchmarks, and a downstream relevance suite. if int8 shows regressions, try selective mixed precision (e.g., keep attention/QK/ln in fp16). :clipboard:

sasha: gguf hybrid is a good low-risk fallback — quantize most weights but keep layernorms, final projection, and softmax keys in fp16. tends to cut size/memory and keeps behavior stable. we'll prefer per-channel quant where infra allows. I'll prepare gguf build scripts.

liam: hardware matrix note: H100 -> prefer fp8 kernel when available (better perf/latency). A100/RTX -> int8 often has better optimized kernels. CPU/dedicated tiny nodes -> gguf for lower mem. include KV cache memory checks for each config (gguf can reduce resident memory).

nate: quick smoke checklist I'll run and push results here: 
```
# 1) Baseline fp16
python eval.py --model /mnt/models/nova-13b-c/fp16 --suite evalsets/relevance.json --out baseline.json
# 2) int8 PTQ (per-channel)
python quantize.py --model /mnt/models/nova-13b-c/fp16 --mode ptq-int8 --calib 512 --out /tmp/nova-int8.gguf
python eval.py --model /tmp/nova-int8.gguf --suite evalsets/relevance.json --out int8.json
# 3) gguf hybrid (preserve layernorms + final proj)
python quantize.py --mode hybrid --preserve layernorm,final_proj --out /tmp/nova-hybrid.gguf
python eval.py --model /tmp/nova-hybrid.gguf --suite evalsets/relevance.json --out hybrid.json
# 4) latency & cost
loadgen --model /tmp/.. --concurrency 8 --out perf.json
python cost_calc.py --perf perf.json --tokens 1e6 --out cost_est.json
```
Include short-context vs long-context slices and code vs prose samples in the evals.

maya: gating suggestions: delta EM/ROUGE <= 3% absolute, PPL change <= 5%, latency P95 <= 1.2x baseline, and no new safety/hallucination failures on our safety suite. also require token-per-dollar calc for each variant. any objections?

jordan: add a tiny synthetic diagnostic set for numeric reasoning and long-context edgecases. if those fail even slightly, escalate to a targeted calibration (more samples or per-channel for the offending layer).

sasha: also record failure-by-slice and attach example prompts + model outputs to the rollout issue. that helps identify whether attention/kv quantization or MLP weights are the culprit. I'll wire a small script to diff outputs and auto-generate examples.

liam: run both per-channel and per-tensor for gguf on a small sample — per-channel is safer but bigger. record file sizes and load times. I'll own the hw routing matrix mapping (config -> preferred kernel).

calib-bot: calibration job queued: job_id=cb-20260314-07, model=nova-13b-c, mode=ptq-int8, samples=1024, owner=@nate. logs: https://ci/internal/calib/cb-20260314-07

nate: starting int8 PTQ run now (monitoring cb-20260314-07). will post a compact result table by EOD with PPL/ROUGE/latency/cost for fp16, int8, hybrid. tagging infra labels `exp/13b/quant/{ptq-int8,fp8,hybrid}` so traces are queryable. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

maya: owner assignments: nate -> PTQ runs + result table, jordan -> eval suite curation + synthetic diagnostics, sasha -> gguf build scripts + diff tool, liam -> hw routing matrix + perf guidance. I'll open the rollout issue and link results. :thumbsup:

jordan: small ask: include tokens/sec-per-dollar in the result table to make tradeoffs obvious.

sasha: I'll push initial gguf per-channel & per-tensor scripts to tools/quant in infra and share PR link here when ready.

maya: great, thanks all. will reconvene after results.
